explain.say: Each cluster has a negative electric charge on its surface. Like charges repel, so the clusters push each other away and stay spread out.

faq.a: The casein clusters in fresh milk all carry a negative charge, so they repel each other and stay evenly spread out.
Bacteria in the milk feed on its sugar, lactose, and make lactic acid. Once enough acid builds up, the proteins clump together.
asks: Why does milk go lumpy when it goes off?

faq.q: How is cheese made from curdled milk?
faq.a: Cheese makers add bacteria and an enzyme called rennet to make the milk curdle, then cut, drain and press the curds and often leave them to age.

faq.q: Why does milk curdle in hot coffee?
faq.a: Coffee is a little acidic and very hot. If the milk is already slightly sour, the heat and acid together make its proteins clump.
asks: Why did my milk curdle in tea?

faq.a: Milk that has curdled because it went off should not be drunk. Milk soured on purpose with safe bacteria, like yoghurt or buttermilk, is fine.

facts: About 80 percent of the protein in cow's milk is casein.
Casein clumps together when milk becomes acidic enough, at about pH 4.6.

quiz.say: Why does a squeeze of lemon make warm milk curdle?
quiz.show: Why does a squeeze of lemon make warm milk curdle?

options.show: Its acid cancels the charges keeping the proteins apart

quiz.why: Acid neutralises the negative charges on the casein clusters, so they clump into curds.

wrong.0: A little lemon juice barely changes the temperature; the acid does the work.
wrong.2: Lemon juice contains no cheese; it makes the milk's own protein clump.
